children: unveiled its Zhenwu V900 AI chip on Tuesday and set a target of more than 20 GW of global data center capacity by 2032, as the Chinese technology giant outlined an expansion across AI models, chips and infrastructure.

The V900, developed by Alibaba's T-Head semiconductor unit, delivers three times the performance of its predecessor, the M890, according to the company. A single cluster can support up to 500,000 chips for training and inference of advanced AI models, while mass production and commercial release are planned for Q1 2027.

Speaking at Alibaba Cloud's Apsara Conference in Hangzhou, Wu said the Qwen team is working on model architecture and data optimization to handle "more complex, longer-horizon tasks" and advance toward artificial superintelligence. The upcoming Qwen 4.5 and Qwen 5 models are expected to scale to 5T to 10T parameters.

Alibaba's current flagship model, Qwen 3.8 Max, has 2.4 trillion parameters, meaning the planned model would be roughly two to four times larger. Wu said Alibaba's proprietary M890 AI supernode already handles inference for models above 2 trillion parameters, a capability he said only "a handful of companies globally" possess.
The Qwen team has made "meaningful progress" on recursive self-improvement, Wu said, with models identifying limitations, designing experiments, and synthesizing data to drive self-evolution.
